extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans and professional stand-up comedians
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and informal standards for judging a club stand-up comedian's stature and skill, as discussed in an obituary/critique of Greg Giraldo. Focuses on what fellow performers and industry insiders consider markers of a great club comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer recognition / 'killing in New York'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Killing in New York means winning over those other comedians looming in the back of the room."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect from fellow performers—especially in NYC clubs where other comedians are present—is presented as a top marker of success; winning over peers in the room is more valued than merely pleasing the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to get laughs from road/unsophisticated audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: "Success on the road is seen as a matter of getting laughs from the unsophisticated audiences of small city clubs and college amphitheaters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A working comedian's success includes consistently making diverse, less-cultivated crowds laugh (road/college/small-club audiences), not just impressing insiders or TV viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence, toughness, and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: "He was smart, he was tough, he was original. The phrase 'comic’s comic' gets tossed around, but Giraldo was the real deal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal traits — clever writing/insight, resilience onstage, and original voice — are core qualitative criteria for being a top club comedian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heckler handling / quickness and improvisational crowd control
rubrics_metrics.description: "He was a Harvard Law grad who was streetwise enough to demolish a heckler... you get a sense of how quick he was in this exchange with a humbled Denis Leary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to respond quickly and decisively to hecklers or unexpected audience interruptions is highlighted as an important performance skill; example video referenced as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form roast skill versus long-form headlining
rubrics_metrics.description: "There was no disputing that he was good at it [roasts]... but four minutes of roasting isn’t starring in a sitcom or headlining Carnegie Hall."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mastery of short, punchy insult-roast segments from skills needed to sustain longer sets, star in sitcoms, or headline large venues; excellence in one format doesn't automatically translate to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast/hired-gun excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: "He made his reputation on television as a hired gun on Comedy Central’s roasts... he’d make 19 out of 20—and Giraldo was always the best on those shows."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being the standout performer in roast settings (sharp insults, timing, and audience-hit-rate) is a specific, recognized metric of comedic skill even if it's a narrow specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-media marketability / TV-friendly traits
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whatever traits mass media success requires of a comedian, either Giraldo lacked them or producers never knew what to do with his talent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and the mass-media market look for certain (often unstated) traits—persona, image, adaptability—that affect a comedian’s ability to translate club success into TV/film/ sitcom opportunities; lack of these can limit wider success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity and consistent high quality
rubrics_metrics.description: "And that’s what Greg Giraldo did for the last 17 years... one of the two or three best club comedians..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained excellence over many years and consistent placement among the top peers are cited as evidence of elite status in the club circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-taking and navigating controversy / identity framing
rubrics_metrics.description: "After his 2007 evisceration of Flavor Flav, he may have taken some heat for making racial jokes... he started being introduced as 'Latino comedian Greg Giraldo,' I imagine to give himself the leeway to make fun of Latinos (and everyone else)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willingness to push boundaries and manage the fallout—through self-branding or other strategies—is a measurable aspect of a comedian’s approach; how one frames identity can affect perceived license to joke about sensitive topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to perform successfully for unfamiliar or unsupportive audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: "...despite neither the audience nor the roastee knowing who the hell he was..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performing strongly even when the crowd is not familiar with you or potentially unsympathetic (e.g., roastee or mainstream TV audience) is highlighted as an important indicator of professional competence.
